assumptions: decision: do NOT configure waypoint.sink; record the abstention instead; decided by human at fleet CONFIRM. Rationale given: no sink infrastructure exists to point at, so wiring one would be speculative. This lane did not re-open that fork.

The deliverable shape is abstention-disclosure: an ADR, and only an ADR (docs/knowledge/decisions/0033-waypoint-sink-abstention.md). An AGENTS.md note was considered and rejected because the abstention is met in fleet lane output rather than while reading AGENTS.md, and a second copy of the reasoning is one more thing to drift out of sync with the ADR.

harness.config.json is unchanged and gains no `waypoint` key; `git diff --stat harness.config.json` is empty. Verified against the known stripped-key trap: `waypoint` is NOT one of the keys the schema silently strips -- the shared loader declares it as a tolerant passthrough precisely so it does not trip the stripped-key warning, and loadWaypointConfig reads parsed.waypoint straight off the parsed file. So the abstention is a genuine absence, not a schema-path bug documented as if it were a choice.

The revisit condition recorded in the ADR is what the CLI's `ship` block requires, read from @harness-engineering/cli@12.10.0 (WaypointShipConfigSchema): a service url, an outpost id, a project id, and a PNYON_WAYPOINT_INGEST_TOKEN supplied from the environment (a committed token is disqualifying on its own). transport accepts exactly one value, "spool", which writes only to a repo-local .harness/spool/. An initial draft listed three prerequisites and omitted `url`; review caught the overstatement and all four artifacts were corrected together.

`harness waypoint record-provenance` was run unconditionally against this file and its exact output is quoted in the lane report. Its output is the behaviour being documented, so the run is evidence rather than ceremony.

This file uses the camelCase key `planArtifact` as specified by the lane brief. The sibling docs/changes/1074-history-module-headroom/provenance.json uses snake_case `plan_artifact`; nothing parses either key (the CLI reads only `slug`/`item`), so the inconsistency is cosmetic and is reported rather than silently normalised across existing files.

Review (harness-code-reviewer, adversarial on factual overstatement) returned 0 critical / 3 important / 5 suggestion. All three importants were prose-accuracy defects in the ADR and were fixed before commit: (1) the revisit list omitted the required `url` and claimed to be the 'literal prerequisites'; (2) 'read by nobody' was false because `harness waypoint status` reads the spool; (3) the 'two downstream capabilities stay cold' claim restated #967's framing as verified fact when no such consumer exists in CLI 12.10.0 -- it is now attributed to the issue and explicitly marked unverified locally. The five suggestions were not actioned: heading casing, the extra `Revisit test` section, an unquoted YAML `number: 0033` (pre-existing convention across 0026-0032; the drift test reads the filename), a plan step that checks files which do not exist in this worktree, and one positive note.

The ADR index README row was added and ts/test/adr-index.test.ts passes (2/2), which is the gate that enforces one row per ADR with a status matching the file's frontmatter. The known-stale-past-0015 note is obsolete: the index was already current through 0032 on this base, and 0033 keeps it current.

ts/node_modules was absent in this fresh worktree; `npm ci` was run before the gates. CI green is NOT claimed -- the four ts/ gates were green locally (build, typecheck, format:check, and 249 test files / 5017 passed / 2 skipped / 0 failed), plus prettier --check and the CI's markdownlint-cli on the changed docs. CI is verified independently.
keyword_rationale: The issue asks for a decision either way and says: 'If no, record the decision so the no-op is not mistaken for a working seam.' The decision was made (do not configure) and is now recorded durably in an indexed, status-tracked, drift-gated ADR that states the expected output and exit code, names it a deliberate abstention, gives a falsifiable three-part revisit test, and names docs/changes/<slug>/provenance.json as the resulting record of fleet activity. Nothing about #967 remains open.
